products.title: Introduction to Sashiko w/ Mary Lee
products.body_html:
Learn Sashiko with Mary Lee!

Sashiko is a traditional Japanese embroidery technique that began as a functional mending method, but which is now also decorative. The primary stitch used is a running stitch, but the way the stitch is made is slightly different from a Western running stitch. Besides learning the Sashiko stitching method, students will learn tips for drawing the grid used for many patterns, four traditional Sashiko patterns, and the way Sashiko stitching can be used for original designs.

Students will stitch five squares of Sashiko that can be turned into coasters or patches or elements in a table runner. We will begin with a basic pattern of crosses (Jyuji-sashi). The second and third patterns are variations of Jyuji-sahsi. The fourth pattern is connected stairs (Dan-tsunagi) which is the foundation for several classic Sashiko patterns. Our final square will be a simple original design we sketch and stitch with Sashiko running stitches and no particular Sashiko pattern.

Ages 18+

Class Level: True Beginner

Learn more about our class levels here.

  • 5 squares of plain cotton or linen fabric cut to 6” x 6” (15cm x 15cm)
  • Sashiko needle(s)
  • One or more skeins/spools of Sashiko thread in a color (or colors) that contrast with the fabric
  • Fine-point disappearing ink fabric marking pen or pencil (water-soluble is preferable) in a color that contrasts with the fabric
  • Needle threader and reading glasses if necessary

You've mastered Sweater School and you're ready to tackle new techniques - join Emily for Sweater School 4! 

In this a 6 session (7 week) class, students will learn:

  • Drop-sleeve, top-down sweater
  • Picking up stitches for shoulders and sleeves
  • Cables, charts, mock cables, moss stitch - buckle up!

This advanced knitting class does require some time intensive homework to stay on track - please reference the class outline below. Students should have already completed Sweater School or completed multiple sweater or knitted garment project(s) on their own. 

Before class, students should buy and wind yarn, and make a gauge swatch - the instructor will work with students remotely for assistance with this part. When signing up for this class, please make sure to use a current email address.

Class Overview

  • Before first class: Make gauge swatch and wet block it then measure it again to determine your gauge and needle size. Carefully mark your determined needle size(s) throughout the pattern.Wind yarn. Cast on stitches required for class.
  • Week 1: Begin short row shaping of the back yoke: German short rows, left and right crosses (mock cables), knit and purl through the back loop. Cables! (3 hours)
    Homework: Continue back yoke chart.
  • Week 2: Continue on back yoke chart. (2 hours)
    Homework: Finish back yoke.
  • Week 3: Pick up stitches for left and right shoulders. (2 hours)
    Homework: Complete left and right shoulders.
  • Week 4: Join the left and front shoulders together, begin working the front of the sweater. (2 hours)
    Homework: Finish front yoke, join in the round.
  • Week 5: BREAK - No class, continue the body of sweater.
  • Week 6 (class 5): Pick up stitches for sleeves, continue in sleeve pattern.
    Homework: Continue on the body and sleeves.
  • Week 7 (class 6): Italian bind off for the body and/or sleeves. Demo for picking up stitches for the folded neckline.

products.title: Intermediate Knitting: Pick n Mix Beanie w/ Morgan
products.body_html:
Join Morgan to knit Klara Nilsson’s Pick n Mix Beanie, an intermediate project that combines stranded colorwork and cables. In this class, students will learn to read a more complex knitting chart that involves cables and stranded colorwork, and how to vary cables (according to four different charts) to create their own Pick n Mix beanie. Beanies are worked in the round, and started from the top down, instead of the more common bottom up! Students can use these skills to make other cabled and colorwork items, and can even match their Pick n Mix Beanie to a Pick n Mix sweater or mitts!

In this class students will learn: 

  • starting a hat from the top down.

  • increasing stitches in a standard pattern in small circumference knitting.

  • how to hold two different yarns at once. 

  • how to read a knitting chart with 2x2 cables and stranded colorwork. 

  • how to combine cables and colorwork. 

  • cabling without a cable needle.

  • knitting 2x2 ribbing in the round. 

  • how to change needle sizes while working in the round.

  • Magic Loop or Double Pointed Needles technique for small circumference knitting. 

Students will have knitting homework to continue/complete between sessions in order to be prepared for the subsequent class
